title: \noindent Remark
body_md:
\label{Rem.2}
Collecting the main result in \cite{Ding4} and
Theorem~\ref{maintheorem} in the present paper, we precisely characterize the global existence range
$0<\varepsilon_0<\varepsilon_k^*$ and finite-time blowup range
$\varepsilon_k^*\le\varepsilon_0<1$.
head: environment

label: Rem.3
title: \noindent Remark
body_md:
\label{Rem.3}
Consider the small data solution problem for the 2D quasilinear wave equation
\begin{equation}\label{quasi-0}
\text{$\sum_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2g^{\alpha\beta}(\partial v)\partial_{\alpha\beta}^2 v=0$ with $(v,\partial_t v)(1,x)=\delta(v_0(x),v_1(x))$},
\end{equation}
where $(v_0, v_1)(x)\in C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$ and $\delta>0$ is small.
Assume that for small $\partial v$,
\begin{equation}\label{H-01}
\displaystyle g^{\alpha\beta}(\partial v)=m^{\alpha\beta}+\sum_{\kappa=0}^{2} g^{\alpha\beta,\kappa}\partial_\kappa v+\sum_{\kappa,\varsigma=0}^2h^{\alpha\beta,\kappa\varsigma}\partial_\kappa v\partial_\varsigma v+O(|\partial v|^3),
\end{equation}
where $m^{\alpha\beta}$ denotes the Minkowski metric, $g^{\alpha\beta,\kappa}$
and $h^{\alpha\beta,\kappa\varsigma}$ are constants.
It is shown in \cite{Ali3} that the problem \eqref{quasi-0} admits a global smooth solution $v$ satisfying $|\partial v|\le C\delta(1+t)^{-1/2}$ when both the first and the second null conditions hold (i.e.,
$\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\kappa=0}^2g^{\alpha\beta,\kappa}\omega_\alpha\omega_\beta\omega_\kappa\equiv0$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\kappa,\varsigma=0}^2 h^{\alpha\beta,\kappa\varsigma}\omega_\alpha\omega_\beta\omega_\kappa\omega_\varsigma\equiv0$
for $\omega_0=-1$ and $(\omega_1,\omega_2)\in\mathbb S$, respectively).
Otherwise, if either the first or the second null condition fails,
under the generic non-degenerate assumption on $(v_0(x),v_1(x))$, then $v$ blows up in finite time (see \cite{Ali1} and \cite{Ali2}).


For the short pulse problem considered here, no additional generic non-degeneracy assumption is needed for $\varepsilon_k^* \leq \varepsilon_0 < 1$ except the usual condition $\phi_1 \not\equiv 0$.

label: eq:LT
title: Proof
body_md:
From \eqref{LTTT}, one has $g(\tilde{T}, \tilde{T}) = 1$, which implies
	$1 = g_{ij}\tilde{T}^i\tilde{T}^j = \big(1 + O(M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)})\big)\sum_{i=1}^2|\tilde{T}^i|^2$.
	This leads to
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:LT}
	|\tilde{T}^i|, \, |\mathring{L}^i| \leq 1 + O(M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}).
	\end{equation}
	
	Moreover, using the identity $|\slashed{d}x^i|^2 = \slashed{g}^{ab}\slashed{d}_a x^i\slashed{d}_b x^i = g^{ii} + (g^{0i})^2 - (\tilde{T}^i)^2$, together with \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions} and \eqref{eq:LT}, we arrive at
	\[
	|\slashed{d}x^i| \lesssim 1.
	\]
	
	In addition, by \eqref{LeL} and \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions}, one has $|\mathring{L}(\varrho\check{L}^i)| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}$. Integrating $\mathring{L}(\varrho\check{L}^i)$ along the integral curves of $\mathring{L}$ and using the relation $\check{T}^i = -g^{0i} - \check{L}^i$, we further obtain
	\[
	|\check{L}^i| + |\check{T}^i| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}.
	\]
	
	From the condition $g_{ij}\big(\check{T}^i - \frac{x^i}{\varrho}\big)\big(\check{T}^j - \frac{x^j}{\varrho}\big)=1$, one gets
	\[
	\left(g_{ij}\omega^i\omega^j\right)\frac{r^2}{\varrho^2} - \left(2g_{ij}\check{T}^i\omega^j\right)\frac{r}{\varrho} + g_{ij}\check{T}^i\check{T}^j - 1 = 0.
	\]
	Thus,
	\begin{equation}\label{rrho}
	\check{\varrho}= \frac{r}{\varrho} - 1 = \frac{1 - g_{ij}\omega^i\omega^j - g_{ij}\check{T}^i\check{T}^j + 2g_{ij}\check{T}^i\omega^j}{\sqrt{g_{ij}\omega^i\omega^j - (g_{ij}\omega^i\omega^j)(g_{ab}\check{T}^a\check{T}^b) + (g_{ij}\check{T}^i\omega^j)^2} + g_{ij}\omega^i\omega^j - g_{ij}\check{T}^i\omega^j}.
	\end{equation}
	This implies $|\check{\varrho}| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}$,
	and hence, by the definition of $\upsilon$ in \eqref{omega}, it holds that
	\[
	|\upsilon| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}.
	\]
On the other hand, from \eqref{lmu}, \eqref{GT} and \eqref{Lchi'}, we have
	\begin{equation}\label{YCao-1}
 \begin{split}
	&|\mathring{L}\mu| \lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k} + M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0}\mu, \\
	&|\mathring{L}(\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})| \lesssim M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0} + (\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})^2 + M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0}|\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}}|,
\end{split}
	\end{equation}
	which lead to $|\mu| \lesssim M^{k+1}$ and $|\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}}| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}$.

label: prop:higher-order-L-infty-estimates
title: \noindent Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{Step 1.} The case of $Z = R$ for all $Z$

\vskip 0.1 true cm

When $\alpha = 0$, the estimate $|\check{\mathscr{X}}|\lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}$ directly follows from \eqref{eq:lower-order-Linfty-estimates}.
Using \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions}, Lemma \ref{lem3.4}, and Proposition \ref{prop:lower-order-Linfty-estimates}, one can obtain
the estimates for ${}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}$, ${}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}_L$, ${}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}_T$, ${}^{(T)}\slashed{\pi}$, and ${}^{(T)}\slashed{\pi}_L$.

Additionally, from \eqref{eq:1-f} and \eqref{R}, we know $|R\check{L}^i| \sim |\slashed{d}\check{L}^i|$. The estimate of $R\check{L}^i$ then follows from \eqref{deL}, which in turn allows us to treat $R\check{T}^i$, $R\upsilon$ and $R\check{\varrho}$. Hence, $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R} \slashed{d} x^j = \slashed{d}(\Omega^i - g_{aj}\tilde{T}^a\Omega^j\tilde{T}^i)$ can be estimated.

For $R\mu$, it satisfies the equation
\begin{equation*}
\mathring{L}(R\mu) = {}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}_L^X \slashed{d}_X\mu + R\big(-\frac{1}{2}\mu G_{\mathring{L}\mathring{L}}^\gamma \mathring{L}\varphi_\gamma - \mu G_{\tilde{T}\mathring{L}}^\gamma \mathring{L}\varphi_\gamma + \frac{1}{2}G_{\mathring{L}\mathring{L}}^\gamma T\varphi_\gamma\big)
\end{equation*}
by \eqref{lmu}, which implies $|\mathring{L}R\mu| \lesssim M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0}|R\mu|+M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}$ with the help of \eqref{GT}. Integrating along the integral curves of $\mathring{L}$ yields $|R\mu| \lesssim M^{k+1}$.

Therefore, \eqref{eq:higher-order-L-infty-estimates} holds for $|\alpha|=0$ and $|\beta|=1$.

For general $\alpha$ and $\beta$, one can use the induction argument. Assume that \eqref{eq:higher-order-L-infty-estimates} holds 
for all vector fields $R$ and $|\alpha|=|\beta|-1=p \leq N-3$, then it follows from \eqref{Lchi'} that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
|\mathring{L}R^{p+1}(\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})| &\lesssim |[\mathring{L}, R^{p+1}](\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})| + |R^{p+1}\mathring{L}(\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})| \\
&\lesssim M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0} + M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0}|R^{p+1}(\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})|,
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
which yields $|R^{p+1}(\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr{X}})| \lesssim M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)}$. Thus, the estimates of $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1} {}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}$, $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1} {}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}_{\mathring{L}}$, $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1} {}^{(T)}\slashed{\pi}$, $R^{p+2}\check{L}^i$, $R^{p+2}\check{T}^i$, $R^{p+2}\check{\varrho}$, $R^{p+2}\upsilon$ and $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1}\slashed{d}x^i$ are obtained by Lemma \ref{lem3.4}, \eqref{deL}, 
and the definitions of $\check{T}^i$, $\check{\varrho}$ and $\upsilon$.

Analogously,
$|\mathring{L}R^{p+2}\mu| \lesssim M^k\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0}|R^{p+2}\mu|+M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}$
holds by \eqref{lmu} and \eqref{GT}, which  allows us to further estimate $R^{p+2}\mu$, $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1} {}^{(R)}\slashed{\pi}_T$ and $\slashed{\mathcal{L}}_{R}^{p+1} {}^{(T)}\slashed{\pi}_{\mathring{L}}$.

\vskip 0.1 true cm
	
\textbf{Step 2.} The general case of $Z \in \{\mathring{L}, T, R\}$

\vskip 0.1 true cm


In this case, one can use \eqref{Lchi'}, \eqref{Tchi'}, \eqref{TL}, \eqref{LeL}, \eqref{lmu} and the estimates from Step 1 to prove the results
in \eqref{eq:higher-order-L-infty-estimates}. Since the proof procedure is rather analogous that in \cite[Propositions 6.2 and 6.3]{Ding3},
we omit the details here.

label: LXi
title: Proof
body_md:
Note that $\Theta$ is a vector field on $S_{s, u}$ and one has
	\begin{equation}\label{LXi}
	\mathring L\Theta^X=[T,\mathring L]^X=\big(\mathscr{D}_T\mathring L-\mathscr{D}_{\mathring L}T\big)^X=\slashed d^X\mu+2\mu\zeta^X.
	\end{equation}
	Then
	\[
	\mathring L(\varrho^{-2}|\Theta|^2)=2\varrho^{-2}|\Theta|^2|(\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr X}+\frac12\slashed g^{XX}G_{XX}^\gamma\mathring L\varphi_\gamma)+2\varrho^{-2}(\slashed d_X\mu
	+2\mu\zeta_X)\Theta^X.
	\]
	This, together with the estimates \eqref{eq:higher-order-L-infty-estimates}, \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions} and \eqref{zeta}, yields
	\begin{equation}\label{Y1}
	|\mathring L(\varrho^{-1}|\Theta|)|\lesssim  M^{k}\delta^{2k(1-\varepsilon_0)-\varepsilon_0} \varrho^{-1}|\Theta|	+ M^k\delta^{k(1-\varepsilon_0)-1}.
	\end{equation}
	Thus \eqref{Xi} is obtained through integrating \eqref{Y1} along the integral curves of $\mathring L$.
head: environment

label: prop:bootstrap-higher-derivatives
title: \noindent Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:bootstrap-higher-derivatives}
Under the bootstrap assumptions \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions},
for small $\delta>0$, the following estimates
hold that for $t_0\leq s<T_\delta$ and $|\alpha|\leq N-2$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bootstrap-higher-derivatives}
\delta^{l+m\varepsilon_k}|Z^\alpha\phi|
\lesssim\delta^{2-\varepsilon_0},
\quad
\delta^{l+m\varepsilon_k}|Z^\alpha\varphi_\gamma|
\lesssim\delta^{1-\varepsilon_0},
\quad \gamma=0,1,2,
\end{equation}
where $Z \in \{ \mathring{L}, T, R \}$, $l$ and $m$
denote the numbers of $T$  and $\mathring{L}$ in $Z^\alpha$, respectively.
Moreover,
\begin{align}
\bigl|
\varrho^{1/2}T\varphi_\gamma(s,u,\vartheta)
-\varrho_0^{1/2}T\varphi_\gamma(t_0,u,\vartheta)
\bigr|
&\lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k},
\label{Tvp}\\
\bigl|
\varrho^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(s,u,\vartheta)
-\varrho_0^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(t_0,u,\vartheta)
\bigr|
&\lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{(k+1)(1-\varepsilon_0)}
\label{r0vp}
\end{align}
with $\varrho=s-u$ and $\varrho_0=t_0-u$.
head: environment

label: barzvp
title: Proof
body_md:
From \eqref{fequation} and Proposition~\ref{prop:higher-order-L-infty-estimates}, we have that for all $|\alpha| \leq N-2$,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\bigl| \mathring{L}{\bar Z}^\alpha \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma + \frac{1}{2\varrho}{\bar Z}^\alpha\underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma \bigr| \\
&= \big|{\bar Z}^\alpha (\mu\slashed\triangle\varphi_\gamma+H_\gamma )+ [\mathring{L}, {\bar Z}^\alpha] \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma
- \sum_{\substack{\alpha_1 + \alpha_2 =\alpha\\ |\alpha_1| > 0}}{\bar Z}^{\alpha_1} \big( \frac{1}{2\varrho} \big){\bar Z}^{\alpha_2} \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma \big| \\
&\lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k-l},
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
where $\bar Z\in\{T, R\}$ and $l$ is the number of $T$ operators in $\bar Z^\alpha$.
Consequently,
\[
\bigl| \mathring{L} \bigl( \varrho^{1/2}{\bar Z}^\alpha \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma \bigr) \bigr|
\lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k-l},
\]
which implies
\[
\bigl| \varrho^{1/2} {\bar Z}^\alpha \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma(s,u,\vartheta) -\varrho_0^{1/2}{\bar Z}^\alpha \underline{\mathring L} \varphi_\gamma(t_0,u,\vartheta) \bigr|
\lesssim M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k-l}.
\]
From this, \eqref{Tvp} and $|{\bar Z}^\alpha T \varphi_\gamma| \lesssim \delta^{-\varepsilon_0-l}$ can be obtained.
Then commuting $T$ with $\bar Z^\alpha$ yields $|T\bar{Z}^\alpha \varphi_\gamma| \lesssim \delta^{-\varepsilon_0-l}$.
In addition, by \eqref{Xi} and \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions}, we deduce
\begin{equation}\label{barzvp}
\Bigl| \frac{\partial}{\partial u}{\bar Z}^\alpha \varphi_\gamma \Bigr|
\lesssim \bigl| T{\bar Z}^\alpha \varphi_\gamma \bigr| + \bigl| \Theta^X \slashed{d}_X {\bar Z}^\alpha \varphi_\gamma \bigr|
\lesssim \delta^{-\varepsilon_0-l}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{YHCC-A1}
\begin{split}
	&\Bigr|\frac{\partial}{\partial u}\bigl(\varrho^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(s, u, \vartheta)-\varrho_0^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(t_0, u, \vartheta)\bigr)\Bigr|\\
\lesssim &|\varrho^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(s, u, \vartheta)-\varrho_0^{1/2}\varphi_\gamma(t_0, u, \vartheta)\Bigr|+O(M^{k+1}\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Integrating \eqref{barzvp} and \eqref{YHCC-A1} from $0$ to $u$ gives $|{\bar Z}^\alpha \varphi_\gamma| \lesssim \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0-l}$ and \eqref{r0vp}, respectively.

We now prove \eqref{eq:bootstrap-higher-derivatives} for $\varphi_\gamma$ by induction on the number of $\mathring{L}$ operator. 
The case of $m=0$ follows by integrating \eqref{barzvp}. For the induction argument, assume that for some integer $p\ge 0$ 
and for all $|\alpha|\leq N-2$ containing at most $p$  $\mathring{L}$'s, it holds
\[
|Z^\alpha\varphi_\gamma|\lesssim\delta^{1-\varepsilon_0-l-m\varepsilon_k},
\]
where $l$ and $m$ are the numbers of $T$ and $\mathring{L}$ operators in $Z^\alpha$, respectively. Let the multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\leq N-3$ contain exactly $p$ $\mathring{L}$'s. By \eqref{fequation}, we get
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
|Z^\beta\mathring L\underline{\mathring L}\varphi_\gamma|
&=\bigl|Z^\beta\bigl(\mu\slashed\triangle\varphi_\gamma+H_\gamma-\frac{1}{2\varrho}\underline{\mathring L}\varphi_\gamma\bigr)\bigr|\\
&\lesssim\delta^{-l-p\varepsilon_k}\bigl(\delta^{-\varepsilon_0}+\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k}M^{k+1}\bigr),
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
which implies
\[
|Z^\beta\mathring L T\varphi_\gamma|\lesssim\delta^{-l-p\varepsilon_k}\bigl(\delta^{-\varepsilon_0}+\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k}M^{k+1}\bigr).
\]
By commuting $T$ with $Z^\beta\mathring L$, one then has
\[
|T Z^\beta\mathring L\varphi_\gamma|\lesssim\delta^{-l-p\varepsilon_k}\bigl(\delta^{-\varepsilon_0}+\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k}M^{k+1}\bigr).
\]
As in~\eqref{barzvp}, we can find
\[
\Bigl|\frac{\partial}{\partial u}Z^\beta\mathring L\varphi_\gamma\Bigr|
\lesssim\delta^{-l-p\varepsilon_k}\bigl(\delta^{-\varepsilon_0}+\delta^{-2\varepsilon_k}M^{k+1}\bigr).
\]
Integrating this with respect to $u$ yields
\[
|Z^\beta\mathring L\varphi_\gamma|\lesssim\delta^{1-\varepsilon_0 -l-(p+1)\varepsilon_k}.
\]
This completes the induction argument and obtains the second bound in~\eqref{eq:bootstrap-higher-derivatives}.

Finally, we turn to the estimate of $\phi$. From the relation $T\phi = \mu \tilde T^i \varphi_i$, one has
$Z^\alpha T\phi = Z^\alpha(\mu \tilde T^i \varphi_i)$. Based on the already obtained bound for $\varphi_i$, we have
$|Z^\alpha T\phi| \lesssim \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0-l-m\varepsilon_k}$.
By commuting $T$ with $Z^\alpha$ and using the induction hypothesis for the lower-order terms of $\phi$, one deduces
$|T Z^\alpha \phi| \lesssim \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0-l-m\varepsilon_k}$.
Then, as in~\eqref{barzvp}, it holds that
\[
\Bigl|\frac{\partial}{\partial u} Z^\alpha \phi\Bigr|
\lesssim \delta^{1-\varepsilon_0-l-m\varepsilon_k}.
\]
Integrating this from $0$ to $u$ yields
$|Z^\alpha \phi| \lesssim \delta^{2-\varepsilon_0-l-m\varepsilon_k}$,
which is just the first estimate in~\eqref{eq:bootstrap-higher-derivatives}.

label: mumin
title: \noindent Proposition
body_md:
Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{Prop.5.1}, for
small $\delta>0$ and any $s\in[t_0, T_\delta)$
such that $\mu_{\min}(s)<1/10$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{mumin}
\mu_{\min}(s)
\gtrsim\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}(T_\delta-s).
\end{equation}
Furthermore, for each
$(u,\vartheta)\in[0,4\delta]\times\mathbb S$,
\begin{equation}\label{Tmu}
(\mu^{-1}T\mu)_+(s,u,\vartheta)
\lesssim
\delta^{-1+\varepsilon_k/2}
(T_\delta-s)^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where $(\mu^{-1}T\mu)_+$ denotes the positive part
of $\mu^{-1}T\mu$.
head: environment

label: DXY-3
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $s\in[t_0, T_\delta)$ such that
$\mu_{\min}(s)<1/10$.
Choose $(u_0,\vartheta_0)\in[0,4\delta]\times\mathbb S$
such that
\[
\mu(s,u_0,\vartheta_0)=\mu_{\min}(s).
\]
By Proposition~\ref{Prop.5.1} and continuity, $\mu$ remains below
$1/10$ along this fixed characteristics for all subsequent
time  and
\[
\mathring L\mu(\tau,u_0,\vartheta_0)\sim-\delta^{-\varepsilon_k},
\qquad s\le\tau<T_\delta.
\]
Thus, for $s<S< T_\delta$, the positivity of
$\mu$ gives
\[
\begin{split}
\mu_{\min}(s)
&=
\mu(S,u_0,\vartheta_0)
-\int_s^S
\mathring L\mu(\tau,u_0,\vartheta_0)\,d\tau\ge-\int_s^{S} \mathring{L}\mu(\bar{s}, u_0, \vartheta_0) \, d\bar{s} \sim \delta^{-\varepsilon_k}(S-s).
\end{split}
\]
Letting $S\to T_\delta-$ yields \eqref{mumin}.

We next estimate the positive part of $\mu^{-1}T\mu$.
For the fixed time $s$, $T=\partial_u-\Theta^X\partial_\vartheta$ can be straighten by setting
\[
\tilde u=u,\quad
\tilde\vartheta=\vartheta+g(s,u,\vartheta),
\]
where
\[
\partial_u g-\Theta^X\partial_\vartheta g=\Theta^X,
\quad
g(s,0,\vartheta)=0.
\]
Due to $T\tilde u=1$ and $T\tilde\vartheta=0$,
we have $T=\partial_{\tilde u}$.

Fix $\tilde\vartheta$ and write
\begin{equation}\label{DXY-3}
f(\tilde u)=(\mu^{-1}T\mu)(s,\tilde u,\tilde\vartheta),
\end{equation}
where the quantity on the right hand side of \eqref{DXY-3} is expressed in
the new coordinates.
If $\max_{[0,4\delta]}f\le0$, then $f_+=0$.
Otherwise, choose $u^*\in[0,4\delta]$ at which
$f$ attains its positive maximum.
If $u^* = 0$, then $(s, u^*, \tilde{\vartheta})$ is a point on the outermost characteristic curve, which implies that $\mu(u^*) = 1$ and $T\mu(u^*) = 0$. This contradicts the assumption $f(u^*) > 0$, and hence $u^* \in (0, 4\delta]$, which yields $f'(u^*) \geq 0$. Therefore, together with the fact that $|T^2\mu| \lesssim \delta^{-2}$ by \eqref{eq:higher-order-L-infty-estimates}, one has
	\begin{equation}\label{muT}
	\bigl(\mu^{-1}T\mu\bigr)(u^*) \leq \sqrt{\dfrac{T^2\mu}{\mu}(u^*)}\lesssim\delta^{-1}\bigl(\mu_{\min}(s)\bigr)^{-1/2}.
	\end{equation}
The maximality of $f(u^*)$ therefore yields
\[
f_+(\tilde u)
\lesssim
\delta^{-1}\mu_{\min}(s)^{-1/2},
\quad 0\le\tilde u\le4\delta.
\]
Note that $\tilde\vartheta$ is arbitrary, returning to the
original coordinates gives
\[
(\mu^{-1}T\mu)_+(s,u,\vartheta)
\lesssim
\delta^{-1}\mu_{\min}(s)^{-1/2}
\]
throughout $[0,4\delta]\times\mathbb S$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{mumin}, we conclude that
\[
(\mu^{-1}T\mu)_+(s,u,\vartheta)
\lesssim
\delta^{-1+\varepsilon_k/2}
(T_\delta-s)^{-1/2}.
\]
This completes the proof.

label: lem:higher_order_L2_estimates_mu
title: \noindent Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At first, suppose $E\neq\varnothing$.
By Proposition~\ref{Prop.5.1}, once $\mu<1/10$ along a fixed
characteristics, it remains below $1/10$ and decreases.
It follows from the definition of $\underline s$ that $
\mu_{\min}(\tau)<1/10$ when
$\underline s<\tau<T_\delta$.
Fix $\underline s<\tau<s< T_\delta$, and choose
$(u_\tau,\vartheta_\tau)\in[0,4\delta]\times\mathbb S$
such that
\[
\mu(\tau,u_\tau,\vartheta_\tau)=\mu_{\min}(\tau).
\]
Integrating along this fixed characteristics and using
Proposition~\ref{Prop.5.1}, we obtain
\[
\begin{split}
\mu_{\min}(\tau)
&=
\mu(s,u_\tau,\vartheta_\tau)
-\int_\tau^s
\mathring L\mu(\xi,u_\tau,\vartheta_\tau)\,d\xi\ge
\mu_{\min}(s)
+c\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}(s-\tau)
\end{split}
\]
for some positive constant $c$.
By continuity of $\mu_{\min}$, the same inequality
holds at $\tau=\underline s$.
Therefore, for $a>1$,
\[
\begin{split}
\int_{\underline s}^s\mu_{\min}^{-a}(\tau)\,d\tau
&\le
\int_{\underline s}^s
\left(
\mu_{\min}(s)
+c\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}(s-\tau)
\right)^{-a}\,d\tau\\
&=
\frac{\delta^{\varepsilon_k}}{c(a-1)}
\big[
\mu_{\min}^{1-a}(s)
-
\left(
\mu_{\min}(s)
+c\delta^{-\varepsilon_k}(s-\underline s)
\right)^{1-a}
\big]\\
&\le
\frac{\delta^{\varepsilon_k}}{c(a-1)}
\mu_{\min}^{1-a}(s),
\end{split}
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:mu_integrability}.

For any $\underline s<s<s'<T_\delta$,
choose $(u_s,\vartheta_s)$ such that
$\mu(s,u_s,\vartheta_s)=\mu_{\min}(s)$.
The decrease of $\mu$ along this characteristics gives $
\mu_{\min}(s')
\le
\mu(s',u_s,\vartheta_s)
\le
\mu(s,u_s,\vartheta_s)
=
\mu_{\min}(s)$.

For $t_0\le s\le\underline s<s'<T_\delta$,
we have $
\mu_{\min}(s')<\frac{1}{10}\le\mu_{\min}(s)$.

For $t_0\le s<s'\le\underline s$, the uniform upper
bound for $\mu$ from
\eqref{eq:lower-order-Linfty-estimates} and Remark~\ref{Rem4.2},
together with $\mu_{\min}(s)\ge1/10$, yields $
\mu_{\min}(s')\lesssim1\lesssim\mu_{\min}(s)$.
Thus \eqref{eq:mu_monotonicity} holds when $E\neq\varnothing$.

If $E=\varnothing$, then $\mu_{\min}\ge1/10$
throughout $[t_0,T_\delta)$.
The same uniform upper bound therefore gives
\[
\mu_{\min}(s')\lesssim1\lesssim\mu_{\min}(s),
\quad
t_0\le s<s'< T_\delta.
\]
This completes the proof.

label: L2L
title: \noindent Lemma
body_md:
\label{L2L}
For a given function $f\in C(\overline{D^{s,u}})$, define
\[
F(s,u,\vartheta)=\int_{t_0}^s f(\tau,u,\vartheta)\,d\tau.
\]
Under the assumptions \eqref{bootstrap-assumptions}, the following
estimate holds for small $\delta>0$:
\begin{equation}\label{Ff}
\|F\|_{s,u}\lesssim\int_{t_0}^s\|f\|_{\tau,u}\,d\tau,
\end{equation}
where $\|F\|_{s,u}$ denotes the $L^2$ norm of $F$ over
$\Sigma_s^u$, as defined in Definition~\ref{3.4}.

label: lem:null-transport
title: \noindent Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:null-transport}
Let $\phi$ be a smooth solution of \eqref{quasi} in the region
with $\mu>0$. Then the following decomposition holds:
\begin{equation}\label{Gtrivp}
\begin{split}
G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\slashed{\triangle}\varphi_\gamma
=&\slashed{\nabla}^X\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma\bigr)
-\bigl(\slashed{\nabla}^XG_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\bigr)
\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma\\
=&G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0\slashed d_Xx^i
\slashed d^X\mathring L\varphi_i
-\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\mathring L_\gamma\bigr)
\tilde T^i\slashed{\triangle}\varphi_i
-g_{\gamma j}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\slashed d_Xx^j\slashed d^X\mathring L\varphi_\alpha\\
&+\slashed\nabla^X\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0
\slashed d_Xx^i\bigr)\mathring L\varphi_i
-\slashed\nabla^X\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\mathring L_\gamma\tilde T^i\bigr)\slashed d_X\varphi_i
-\bigl(\slashed\nabla^XG_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\bigr)
\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma\\
&-\slashed\nabla^X\bigl(g_{\gamma j}
G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\slashed d_Xx^j\bigr)\mathring L\varphi_\alpha.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Set
$
E_0=-G_{X\mathring L}^\gamma\slashed d^X\varphi_\gamma
+\frac{1}{2}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0
\slashed d_Xx^i\slashed d^X\varphi_i
-\frac{1}{2}g_{\gamma j}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\slashed d_Xx^j\slashed d^X\varphi_\alpha$.
Then $\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr X}-E_0$
satisfies the transport equation
\begin{equation}\label{transport}
\begin{split}
&\mathring L\bigl(\varrho^2
\bigl(\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr X}-E_0\bigr)\bigr)\\
=&-\frac{1}{2}\varrho^2
\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\mathring L_\gamma\bigr)
\tilde T^i\slashed\triangle\varphi_i
-\varrho^2\bigl(\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr X}\bigr)^2
+\frac{1}{2}\varrho^2\slashed\nabla^X
\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0\slashed d_Xx^i\bigr)
\mathring L\varphi_i
-\frac{1}{2}\varrho^2\slashed\nabla^X
\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\mathring L_\gamma\tilde T^i\bigr)\slashed d_X\varphi_i\\
&-\bigl(
\frac{1}{2}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\alpha\mathring L\varphi_\alpha
+G_{\tilde T\mathring L}^\alpha\mathring L\varphi_\alpha
-G_{X\mathring L}^\alpha\slashed d^X\varphi_\alpha
+\slashed g^{XX}G_{XX}^\alpha\mathring L\varphi_\alpha
\bigr)
\bigl(\varrho^2\operatorname{tr}\check{\mathscr X}+\varrho\bigr)\\
&-\frac{1}{2}\varrho^2
\bigl(\slashed\nabla^XG_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\bigr)
\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma
-\frac{1}{2}\varrho^2\slashed\nabla^X
\bigl(g_{\gamma j}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\slashed d_Xx^j\bigr)\mathring L\varphi_\alpha\\
&+\mathring L\bigl(\varrho^2G_{X\mathring L}^\gamma
\slashed g^{XX}\bigr)\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma
-\frac{1}{2}\mathring L
\bigl(\varrho^2G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0
\slashed d^Xx^i\bigr)\slashed d_X\varphi_i+\frac{1}{2}\mathring L
\bigl(\varrho^2g_{\gamma j}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\slashed d^Xx^j\bigr)\slashed d_X\varphi_\alpha\\
&+\varrho^2f\bigl(\varphi,\slashed dx,\mathring L^1,\mathring L^2\bigr)
\begin{pmatrix}
\slashed d(\varphi^{k-1})\\
\varphi^{2k-2}\slashed d\varphi
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathring L\varphi\\
\slashed d\varphi
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

label: DXY-4
title: \noindent Remark
body_md:
\label{DXY-4}
It is pointed out that the introduction of the corrector $E_0$ is motivated from \eqref{Gtrivp} and \eqref{Lchi'}.
In addition, the coefficient of the  second-order angular derivative $\slashed\triangle\varphi_i$
in \eqref{transport} contains the crucial factor
$G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^{\gamma}\mathring L_{\gamma}$,
which is regular due to the null condition (see \eqref{gLLL}).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It follows from \eqref{gab} and \eqref{quasi} that
\[
\slashed d^Xx^i\slashed d_X\varphi_i
=-\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\mathring L\varphi_\alpha.
\]
Together with \eqref{pal}, this implies
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\slashed d_X\varphi_\gamma
=&G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\slashed d_Xx^i
\bigl(\delta_\gamma^0\mathring L\varphi_i
-\mu^{-1}\mathring L_\gamma T\varphi_i
+g_{\gamma j}\slashed d^Xx^j\slashed d_X\varphi_i\bigr)\\
=&G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^0
\bigl(\mathring L\varphi_i\slashed d_Xx^i\bigr)
-\bigl(G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma\mathring L_\gamma\bigr)
\tilde T^i\slashed d_X\varphi_i
-g_{\gamma j}G_{\mathring L\mathring L}^\gamma
\bigl(\mathring L^\alpha+2g^{0\alpha}\bigr)
\mathring L\varphi_\alpha\slashed d_Xx^j.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Taking the angular divergence of this identity and applying the chain
rule yield \eqref{Gtrivp}. Substituting \eqref{Gtrivp} into
\eqref{Lchi'} together with the chain rule gives
\eqref{transport}.
